commitResults.messageTitle: Extract user interaction into Ui class
commitResults.messageBody: Move command input, welcome and exit messages, separators, and error display out of MARY. This isolates console interaction while preserving the existing task, parsing, and persistence behavior as the first incremental OOP refactor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task list and storage responsibilities
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce TaskList to own task collection operations and Storage to own loading and saving task records. Update MARY to compose these collaborators while preserving command behavior and persistence format, preparing the next Parser extraction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task command parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Move todo, deadline, and event command validation and construction into Parser while preserving the existing execution loop and user-visible behavior. This isolates command interpretation before introducing executable command objects.
Add the abstract Command contract and ExitCommand, and route bye through Parser and Command execution. This begins the command hierarchy without changing existing chatbot output.
Move list rendering into ListCommand and route list through the command parser, preserving task numbering and empty-list messaging.
Move todo, deadline, and event task creation, validation, persistence, and confirmation output into AddCommand and route those inputs through Parser.
Move delete validation, task removal, persistence, confirmation, and error reporting into DeleteCommand and route delete inputs through Parser.
Move completion status validation, mutation, persistence, and user feedback into MarkCommand for both mark and unmark operations.
Move date parsing and deadline/event date filtering into OnCommand, preserving the existing on command output and validation.

Ensure every input produces an executable Command by adding UnknownCommand, including blank and unsupported input handling. This removes the parser null path and completes the command dispatch contract.

commitResults.messageTitle: Apply SE-EDU style to Java sources
commitResults.messageBody:
Java sources mix compact statements, wildcard imports, and naming
styles, making the code less consistent to read.

Apply the SE-EDU conventions across production and test code. Rename
the entry point to Mary and update Gradle and run instructions so the
PascalCase name works without changing the displayed chatbot name.

Keep command behavior, storage formats, and test assertions unchanged.
Record the verification limits in the test plans: static checks pass,
but JUnit and UI tests remain pending after build approval was declined.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the SE-EDU Java coding skill
commitResults.messageBody:
The project needs a reusable reference for applying SE-EDU Java rules
consistently across production and test code.

Add a project-local skill with the authoritative source, a working
checklist, and the repository-specific documentation and test rules.
Keep it separate from application changes so the guidance can evolve
without mixing policy updates into code commits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require the Java standard in agent instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
Agent instructions do not yet mandate the project Java coding skill.

Require agents to read and apply the skill before Java work and during
final review. Retain the stronger local Javadoc requirements so adopting
the upstream guide does not weaken existing documentation expectations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require the Java skill in Claude instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
Claude imports the shared agent policy but lacks a direct pointer to
the project Java coding skill.

Add that pointer for production and test code. Keep AGENTS.md as the
policy authority rather than duplicating the full standard.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the SE-EDU Git conventions skill
commitResults.messageBody:
The project needs consistent commit explanations and branch names.

Add a project-local skill based on the SE-EDU Git guide. Cover subject
and body conventions, branch naming, focused staging, and verification
of each resulting commit.

Preserve explicit authorization requirements and report blocked tests
honestly so consistent history does not come at the cost of user
control.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require SE-EDU conventions for future commits
commitResults.messageBody:
The shared agent policy requires commit rationale but does not mandate
a consistent Git convention.

Require the SE-EDU Git skill for all future commit preparation, review,
and creation. Keep existing permission and lightweight-tag rules so
the new standard changes commit quality, not authorization.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require the Git skill in Claude instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
Claude needs an explicit pointer to the commit standard alongside the
existing shared policy import.

Require the project Git skill for future commits while keeping the
full rules in one place. This aligns Claude with the shared agent
instructions without duplicating the conventions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace MARY's Unicode banner with an ASCII cat
commitResults.messageBody:
The Unicode banner displays as question marks in some consoles.

Replace it with an ASCII cat and a matching greeting to avoid
Unicode rendering issues. Update the README and UI expectations,
and add a JUnit test for exact, ASCII-only welcome output.

All 53 JUnit tests and seven UI test sessions passed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keyword search for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users must scan the entire task list to locate tasks by description.

Add a find command that displays numbered matches without changing
tasks or saved data. Match literal substrings case-insensitively so
users can search without remembering exact capitalization.

Handle missing keywords and empty results, and document that result
numbers differ from the full-list numbers used to modify tasks.
Add tests for matching, validation, ordering, and persistence safety.

All 62 JUnit tests and nine UI sessions passed with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Checkstyle and fix Java style violations
commitResults.messageBody:
Java coding conventions rely on manual review, allowing style
violations to enter production and test code.

Add Checkstyle 14.1.0 to Gradle check with the AddressBook Level 3
configuration. Fail on warnings and errors without adding suppressions
so the shared SE-EDU rules remain enforceable.

Fix braces, imports, declaration order, fixture visibility, wrapping,
and Javadoc formatting without changing chatbot behavior. Document
how to run the checks and retain the regression session records.

Validation: Java 25 check shadowJar --rerun-tasks passes with zero
Checkstyle violations and all 62 JUnit tests passing. All eight UI
cases pass across nine sessions with matching output and saved data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JavaFX chat interface for MARY
commitResults.messageBody:
MARY exposes its task commands only through a console loop, making
commands and replies harder to use in a desktop workflow.

Add a resizable JavaFX chat window with Send/Enter input, wrapped
replies, command examples, draft-safe suggestions and a close action.
Share the session, parser and storage with the console and route all
command output through Ui to avoid duplicating business logic.

Make the GUI the default launcher and retain --cli for console use.
Configure JavaFX dependencies and platform-specific fat JAR packaging,
keep native caches in the working folder, and document launch steps.

Add shared-session and GUI tests and retain console regression records.
Validation on Windows with Java 25: 67 unit tests, seven GUI tests and
eight console cases pass; Checkstyle reports zero violations. Verify
that the packaged GUI launches and closes normally. Other operating
systems are not tested; the JavaFX unnamed-module warning is recorded.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add varargs support for grouped UI messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Related replies currently require repeated showMessage calls, making
multi-line responses more verbose to maintain.

Add Ui.showMessages(String... messages) and use it for welcome, add,
delete, and mark replies. Delegate each message to showMessage to
preserve ordering, formatting, and console and GUI output routing.

Add four JUnit tests covering empty calls, single and multiple
messages, and existing array arguments. Update the test documentation
and record the complete console regression sessions.

Verification:
- Pass all 71 unit tests and seven GUI tests
- Pass eight UI regression cases across nine sessions
- Pass Checkstyle with zero violations
- Rebuild the fat JAR
